claims.text: Widespread adoption of large language models is hindered by technical, social, ethical, and legal challenges.
Large language models exhibit significant limitations in interpretability.
Large language models suffer from biases in data and model outcomes.
Large language models require high computational resources for operation and deployment.

evidence.description: Attempts to achieve widespread use of LLMs have met numerous challenges encompassing technical, social, ethical, and legal aspects.
The review identifies model interpretability among the key challenges associated with LLMs.
The paper highlights biases in data and model outcomes as critical key issues.
The authors list high computational requirements as a major challenge facing LLMs.

methodologies.name: Structured Taxonomy and Literature Review
methodologies.description: A comprehensive review and taxonomy analyzing challenges, limitations, domain impacts, solutions, and future directions for large language models.

limitations.text: Lack of interpretability in model decision-making.
Presence of systemic biases in training data and generated model outputs.
Ethical concerns regarding data privacy and security during training and deployment.
High computational resource demands for training and running large language models.

future_work.text: Developing techniques to improve the robustness and control of LLMs against biases and quality issues.
Addressing key challenges for the responsible and effective deployment of LLMs in domain-specific applications such as healthcare, law, media, and education.
